items.heading: An Industrial Training Institute Teaches
items.text: An Industrial Training Institute teaches a trade through mostly workshop practice. Government and private ITIs teach the same national syllabus when they are affiliated for that trade.

items.heading: Rules Vary By State
items.text: Rules vary by state and trade, so use this table to know what to ask, not as the final word.

items.heading: A Trade Name Tells
items.text: A trade name tells you little. This table groups trades by sector and gives the entry and length shown in the sources we could read.

visuals.heading: Iti Eligibility: After 8th, 10th, 10th Fail

rows: A smaller set of trades. One government ITI lists Plumber and Sewing Technology as one-year trades for Class 8 pass.
Many popular trades ask for Class 10. In some states the same trade needs Class 8 under the state council (SCVT) and Class 10 with Maths and Science under the national council (NCVT).
Most trades. COPA, Food Production and Food and Beverage Service Assistant list Class 10 pass.
Engineering trades such as Electrician, Fitter and Mechanic Refrigeration and Air Conditioning list Class 10 pass with Science and Maths.
Only the Class 8 trades, if you hold a Class 8 pass. Otherwise clear Class 10 first, through a supplementary attempt or open schooling.
Ask the ITI for its written eligibility list for your trade. Rules differ by state and by institute.
Every trade open to a Class 10 pass is open to you. The ITI checks your Class 10 subjects, not your Class 12 stream.
A commerce student who skipped Science and Maths in Class 10 may be shut out of engineering trades but can still take COPA and service trades. Some newer trades ask for Class 12, so read each notice.
